byteward.title: Wayline robotaxis start paid rides in Port Ellery
byteward.author: Arlo Pennick
body: [f01: Wayline began charging for robotaxi rides in Port Ellery on Saturday.] [f04: The cars have no safety driver behind the wheel.]
[f02: The service launches with 40 cars.] [f03: Its service area covers 31 square miles of the city.] [f05: Rides are available from 6 a.m. to midnight.]

Charging for rides is the step that turns a test into a business. The next few months will show whether people in Port Ellery are ready to pay for a ride with nobody up front, and whether the cars can handle a city's worth of real traffic.

launch-desk.title: Wayline starts paid robotaxi rides in Port Ellery
launch-desk.author: Inez Calder
body: [f01: Wayline has started paid robotaxi service in Port Ellery.] [f06: Fares are $3 to start plus $1.90 per mile.] [f02: The launch fleet is 40 cars.]
[f08: Wayline plans to grow that to 200 cars by mid-2027.] [f07: The company raised $600 million in September.] [f11: It pays the city 25 cents for every ride.]
That's a lot of rides to make the math work.

bench-and-bill.title: Wayline robotaxis begin paid rides in Port Ellery
bench-and-bill.author: Owen Brightwater
body: [f01: Wayline started paid robotaxi rides in Port Ellery on Saturday.] [f04: Its cars run with no safety driver.] The city's permit sets the terms.
[f09: The permit caps Wayline's fleet at 100 cars.] [f15: The city will review the permit in May.]
[f10: Wayline must report any crash to the city within 12 hours.] [f11: It also pays the city a fee of 25 cents per ride.]
The cap is the condition to watch, because any plan to grow the fleet runs straight into it.

ohm-and-bit.title: Wayline's driverless robotaxis start paid rides in Port Ellery
ohm-and-bit.author: Imogen Vale
body: [f01: Wayline's robotaxis began paid rides in Port Ellery on Saturday.] [f04: Nobody sits behind the wheel.] So what's doing the driving?

[f12: Each car carries five lidar sensors, which map the street around it with laser pulses.] [f14: Wayline caps the cars at 45 mph.] That keeps them off fast roads, where the software would have less time to react.
[f13: Remote operators can suggest a route when a car gets stuck, but they can't steer it.] That's a deliberate limit. A laggy connection is a bad way to drive a car.

wirefold.title: Wayline begins paid robotaxi service in Port Ellery
body: Wayline on Saturday began charging for driverless robotaxi rides in Port Ellery, starting with a fleet of 40 cars.
